english.title: Use vehicle to kill / take Schedule 6 wild animal
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), used a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY..), in immediate pursuit of

(A)_[a wild animal]_
(B)_[wild animals]_

included in Schedule 6 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, namely **(..SPECIFY SPECIES..), for the purpose of driving, killing or taking

(C)_[it]_
(D)_[them]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(2)(e) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(ii) Section 21(5) provides that where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each.
(iii) See Section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and Section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(v) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
